newsitem.title: USA: Triton says in talks on Thai natgas supply.
newsitem.headline: Triton says in talks on Thai natgas supply.

text.p: Triton Energy Ltd is currently in talks to sell natural gas from its Block A-18 discovery in the Gulf of Thailand.
"The talks are at a very delicate stage at the moment, so I cannot say too much about them," Triton chief executive Tom Finck told the Howard Weil energy conference on Monday.

Triton expects the field to be producing 300 million cubic feet per day by early in the year 2000 and said that the Thai natgas pipeline operator was set to extend a an offhore pipeline to bring the gas to the port city of Rayong.
It estimates that probable and proven reserves from block A-18 are nine trillion cubic feet of natural gas.
Triton also said that it was currently in the process of refinancing its long-term debt through to the year 2000.
"These high yielding notes will be restructured which will give us higher margins," Finck said, adding that a deal was imminent.
The company plans to sell 10 million barrels of oil per year in 1997 and 18 million in 1998, compared with 5.7 million in 1996.

While most of the additions come from fields in Colombia and the Gulf of Thailand, Triton said that it had entered negotiations for offshore work near Madagascar and onshore Algeria. ((--David Chance, New Orleans newsroom--))
